clue.text: His skill on board may have resulted from a first-rate teacher

definitions.text: His skill on board may have resulted from a first-rate teacher

parts.words: His skill on board may have resulted from a first-rate teacher
parts.note: read literally; the board is a chessboard, and the top chess title is the same two words run together

explanation.surface: A chess player's talent is credited to an excellent tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' sounds like school governance, but it is the chessboard; 'first-rate' is GRAND and 'teacher' MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest title in international chess is held by a player whose board skill is supreme.

clue.text: Balcony set right inside the ship

indicators.note: inside tells us the abbreviation for right goes within the word for the ship

parts.note: a galley is a ship driven by oars

explanation.surface: A balcony has been fitted on the right-hand side within a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a link: R is set inside GALLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery is a raised upper floor in a theatre or church, much like a balcony.

clue.text: Withdrawn as the result of a silly upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for a silly person upside down, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: as a noun, a silly is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone has retreated into themselves after a foolish quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns FOOL to LOOF; 'silly' is a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof is distant and reserved, kept apart from others.

clue.text: Underworld chief has a fervent desire to be contradicted

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
greed is an intense craving

explanation.surface: The lord of Hades is avid to be argued with.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis (Pluto) is the Roman ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To have disagreed is to have opposed or gainsaid what another said.

clue.text: Just open-so have a glass of ale

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: With the door barely open, someone pops in for a quick beer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'a jar' is informal for a drink in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly unlatched stands partly open, the meaning of the word.

clue.text: Lawrence gets the Socialist tied up

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials
taken as written
red is a common word for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Lawrence and a left-winger end up bound together.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence of Arabia was T. E. Lawrence, so his initials TE are used.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal tethered is secured with a rope, that is, fastened or bound.

clue.text: Either way it's direct

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever route you take, it points you somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer someone to a specialist is to send or point them on, a synonym of direct.

clue.text: To agree without reservation

parts.note: two accounts that tally match or agree

explanation.surface: To consent unconditionally.
explanation.walkthrough: TO is given as written; TALLY means 'agree' as in figures that correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something totally means wholly, with no qualification held back.

clue.text: Polly got a new position as a linguist

indicators.note: the letters of the name and verb are given a new position, rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Polly has been appointed as a translator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new position' sounds like a job, but signals that POLLYGOT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fluent in many tongues is a speaker of several languages, a linguist.

clue.text: Dress yourself up, and be quick about it

definitions.meaning: to make an effort to appear well turned out
an old British command to hurry up

explanation.surface: An order to smarten up, and to get a move on.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to appear well dressed and, in dated British usage, to hurry.

clue.text: Show contempt for a loud mouthed yobbo

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a yobbo is British slang for a lout

explanation.surface: Defying the rules is a brash, big-mouthed thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouthed' only completes the surface 'loud-mouthed'; F is forte, loud in music.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout a rule is to disregard it openly and scornfully.

clue.text: It represents a figure in unusual pose

definitions.text: It represents a figure in unusual pose

parts.words: It represents a figure in unusual pose
parts.note: a model or statue made to stand for a person, often stuffed and posed to be burnt or mocked

explanation.surface: Something portrays a person in an odd stance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy or sculpture made in the likeness of a person, such as a Guy burnt on Bonfire Night.

clue.text: Feel sure that Raymond and Albert are shopping

parts.note: to bet on something is to be confident of it
Ray is short for Raymond
Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: Someone is confident that two men are out buying things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopping' is British slang for informing on someone to the police, not buying goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopping someone, in British slang, means grassing on them to the authorities, a treachery.

clue.text: You sign as independent farmers

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: You sign up as freeholding farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically English farmers who owned and worked their own land were small freeholders.

clue.text: Hero's appeal is evergreen

parts.note: O is the cry of someone appealing to another, as in 'O Romeo'
in Greek myth Leander was Hero's lover, who swam the Hellespont to her

explanation.surface: A hero's charm stays fresh for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' is not a brave person but the priestess of the myth; her appeal is 'O Leander!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a poisonous Mediterranean shrub that keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Retired cleric and bishop join forces, so it's said

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the abbreviation for the cleric is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to ally is to join forces

explanation.surface: A pensioned-off priest teams up with a bishop, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like a description of the cleric but turns REV into VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done verbally is done in speech, in spoken words rather than writing.

clue.text: Vessel I dare to storm when he's in command

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: a storm throws the letters into turmoil, scrambling them

explanation.surface: A pirate dares to attack a ship while he is the captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to storm' turns I DARE into ADIER; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An army officer who leads a brigade is the one in charge of it.

clue.text: Bound to attend a series of lee

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Bound to attend a series of lee (2,6)': cut short or garbled after 'series of' (probably 'lectures'); no scan and a search gives no fuller text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Bound to attend a series of lee

clue.text: Repeated claim that things are finished is exaggerated

parts.words: Repeated claim that things are finished
parts.note: said twice, 'it's over', meaning finished

parts.words: Repeated claim that things are finished
parts.note: and again, 'it's done', also meaning finished

explanation.surface: Insisting again and again that it's all over is going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words for 'finished' are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance overdone is overplayed, taken too far, much like overstated.

clue.text: An antiquated prison? The devil it is!

parts.note: antiquated means old
the nick is British slang for prison or a police station

explanation.surface: An ancient jail is a hellish place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The nick' is British slang for jail; Old Nick is a folk name for Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a traditional nickname for Satan.

clue.text: Assume a, if you have it not" (Hamlet, Act III)

definitions.text: Assume a, if you have it not" (Hamlet, Act III)

parts.words: Assume a, if you have it not" (Hamlet, Act III)
parts.note: Hamlet's line to his mother Gertrude has a gap where a word for moral goodness belongs

explanation.surface: A quotation from Hamlet with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in Hamlet's advice to Gertrude: pretend to goodness even if you lack it.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the Shakespeare line means moral excellence or chastity.

clue.text: Busily occupied-doubtless in arranging the wedding

definitions.meaning: busy, tied up, as a telephone line or a person can be
a couple arranging their wedding are betrothed

explanation.surface: Someone is busy, no doubt planning the marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both busy with something and betrothed to be married.

clue.text: Charitable contribution from the same country

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A gift to charity comes from one's own land.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the abbreviation of ditto, meaning 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift made to a good cause is a contribution to it.

clue.text: Examine a seedy coat

parts.note: to test is to examine

explanation.surface: Inspect a shabby jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy' looks like shabby but means 'of a seed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use the term for the hard outer skin covering a seed.

clue.text: Trite quotation from a paper from the riff-raff

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
a tag is a hackneyed phrase or saying

explanation.surface: A tired quotation from a tabloid comes from the rabble.
explanation.walkthrough: TAG is said to come from RAG, so RAG goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'ragtag and bobtail' means the rabble, the lowest classes.

clue.text: It is not vulgar and corrupt

parts.note: in contracted speech 'it' shrinks to the single letter, as in 'twas
ain't is a nonstandard, vulgar form of is not

explanation.surface: It isn't crude, and it's dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: Together the pieces give 'tain't, a dialect contraction of 'it is not'.
explanation.definitionFit: To taint is to contaminate or spoil, morally or physically.

clue.text: Its driver has a duty to take one

definitions.text: Its driver has a duty to take one

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cabbie is obliged to pick up a passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a cab whose driver must take a fare, while TAX (duty) takes I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A cab for hire is driven by someone bound to carry a passenger.

clue.text: Sadie produced some original thoughts

indicators.note: produced suggests the name has been worked into something new, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Sadie came up with fresh notions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' signals rearranging the letters of SADIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions or concepts conceived in the mind are new thoughts.

clue.text: True; I make notes to acquire understanding

parts.note: real means true or genuine
to sing is to produce musical notes

explanation.surface: Honestly, I write things down in order to learn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make notes' sounds like note-taking but means singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Realising something is coming to grasp it, gaining awareness.

clue.text: Improved organisation of a male editor

indicators.note: organisation of means the letters are arranged afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: Things got better once a man ran the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation of' looks like management, but signals rearranging A MALE EDITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions ameliorated have been made better, enhanced.
